note: One entry per code (SPEC §20.3-20.4). {name} is filled from the fault's facts. Fixes list the no-terminal way first (D22); a command is something the person copies and runs themselves, with what it does and how to undo it (D49, D53). Sources: the 2026-09-29/30 case on the Mint box (journal), Debian/Ubuntu/Mint documentation as cited per fix.

G101.title: The graphics driver is installed but not running
G101.meaning: The NVIDIA driver ({driver}) is installed, but it isn't loaded for the running kernel ({kernel}). The screen falls back to a basic mode and the assistant can't use the graphics card.

causes.unsigned: Secure Boot is on and the driver isn't signed with a key this computer trusts.
causes.not_built: The driver was never built for kernel {kernel}.
causes.file_damaged: The driver file for kernel {kernel} reads back damaged. That usually means the disk or its connection had trouble, not the driver itself.
causes.driver_refused: The driver started but refused to run (see the evidence).
causes.unknown: The cause isn't one this tree knows yet; the evidence is recorded in full.

unsigned.words: Let the driver's key be enrolled at the next start.
steps: Open Driver Manager and reinstall the recommended driver; it asks for a one-time password.
Restart. A blue screen titled "Perform MOK management" appears: choose Enroll MOK, Continue, Yes, type that password, then Reboot.
unsigned.verify: the driver loads after the restart (nvidia-smi shows the card)

not_built.words: Build the driver for this kernel.
steps: Open Driver Manager, pick the recommended driver again, click Apply Changes, then restart.
not_built.command: sudo apt install linux-headers-{kernel} && sudo dkms autoinstall -k {kernel}
not_built.explain: Installs the kernel's build files and builds every add-on driver (here: NVIDIA) for kernel {kernel}. Changes only driver files for that kernel.
not_built.undo: Nothing to undo: it builds what should have been there.
not_built.verify: dkms status lists {module} as installed for {kernel}

file_damaged.words: First make sure the disk is healthy (ask: is my disk OK?). Then put a fresh copy of the driver in place.
file_damaged.explain: Builds the NVIDIA driver again for kernel {kernel} and replaces the damaged copy. Nothing else changes.
file_damaged.undo: Nothing to undo: it's the same driver version.
file_damaged.verify: after a restart, nvidia-smi shows the card

driver_refused.words: Start the previous kernel, which worked, while this is looked into.
steps: Restart. When the menu appears (hold Shift, or tap Esc, while the computer starts), choose Advanced options, then the older kernel.
driver_refused.verify: the driver loads on the older kernel

unknown.words: Start the previous kernel, and share the report (cinminai-diag report) with whoever helps.

S301.title: An installed kernel has no graphics driver
S301.meaning: Kernel {kernels} is installed but the NVIDIA driver isn't built for it. Starting that kernel would leave the screen in basic mode.

causes.not_built: The driver wasn't built when the kernel was installed (missing build files, or the build failed).

not_built.words: Build the driver for that kernel before restarting into it.
not_built.command: sudo apt install linux-headers-{kernel} && sudo dkms autoinstall -k {kernel}
not_built.explain: Installs the kernel's build files and builds the NVIDIA driver for kernel {kernel}. Nothing changes for the kernel you're running now.
not_built.verify: dkms status lists the driver as installed for {kernel}

I301.title: A disk's connection is reporting errors
I301.meaning: The connection to {disk_words} failed {exceptions} times: commands sent to the disk failed ({failed}) and the link was reset. The errors point at {signal}. Failed writes can leave files damaged.

causes.one_kernel: It happens with kernel {kernels_bad}, not with {kernels_clean}. Newer kernels send bigger pieces of data at a time (failed pieces here: up to {largest_failed_kib} KiB); an older disk or a borderline cable can choke on them.
causes.every_kernel: It happens with every kernel, so it's the hardware: the cable, the port, the power plug, or the disk.

one_kernel.words: Switch to the kernel that works (Update Manager, View, Linux kernels). Until then, make this kernel send smaller pieces to the disk, the way older kernels do.
one_kernel.explain: Limits each write to {disk} to 1280 KiB (it's {max_sectors_kb} now). Nothing is written to the disk by this. It lasts only until the next restart, so don't restart after it.
one_kernel.verify: no new errors for the disk in the next heavy copy or update
one_kernel.source: Linux block layer (queue/max_sectors_kb); the 2026-09-30 case, PLAN D52

every_kernel.words: Check the disk's own health record, then the cable.
steps: Open Disks, choose the disk, open the menu (⋮) and choose SMART Data & Self-Tests.
If "UDMA CRC Error Count" goes up over a few days: replace the SATA cable and use another port.
If reallocated, pending or uncorrectable sectors go up: the disk is wearing out. Copy your important files elsewhere now.
every_kernel.verify: no new link errors after the change

I302.title: Writing to the disk failed
I302.meaning: Some writes to the disk failed{aborted_words}. Files written at that time may be damaged, and the system may switch the disk to read-only to protect it.

causes.write_errors: Writes failed because the disk's connection had errors.
causes.read_only_now: The system disk ({device}) is read-only right now: nothing can be saved, updates and drivers can't install, and USB sticks show as read-only too.

write_errors.words: Copy your important files somewhere safe, then let the disk check run at the next start.
steps: Restart normally (from the menu, not the power button).
If a text screen ends with (initramfs), type the command below and press Enter, then type exit.
write_errors.explain: Checks and repairs the disk's filing records. It can't bring back the contents of files that weren't written; reinstall or re-copy those.

read_only_now.words: Don't keep working on a read-only disk. Restart from the menu so the disk check can run.
steps: Save what you can to a USB stick on another computer if it matters.
Restart from the menu. If the (initramfs) screen appears, type the command and press Enter, then exit.
read_only_now.explain: Checks and repairs the disk's filing records at start.
read_only_now.verify: after the restart, saving a file works

S401.title: The problems follow one kernel
S401.meaning: Kernel {kernel} had problems in {bad_boots} of {boots_on_kernel} starts; kernel {good_kernels} had none on this computer. A newer kernel isn't always better for older hardware.

causes.kernel_regression: Something in kernel {kernel} doesn't suit this computer.

kernel_regression.words: Switch to the long-term kernel, without the terminal.
steps: Open Update Manager, then View → Linux kernels.
Install the long-term kernel series (on Mint 22: 6.8, supported to 2029), or keep {good_kernel}.
Remove kernel {kernel} in the same window, then restart.
kernel_regression.verify: uname -r shows the kernel you chose, and the problems are gone
kernel_regression.source: Linux Mint user guide, Update Manager; the 2026-09-30 case

kernel_regression.words: For one start only: pick the kernel at the start menu.
steps: Restart. Hold Shift (or tap Esc) while the computer starts, choose Advanced options, then {good_kernel}.
kernel_regression.explain: Shows which kernel is running now. It only reads.

H401.title: The computer didn't shut down cleanly last time
H401.meaning: The last session ({ended}) ended without a shutdown: a crash, a power cut, or the power button held down. That can damage files that were being written.

causes.unclean: The previous session's record stops without a shutdown.

unclean.words: When the computer freezes, try the keyboard before the power button.
steps: Press Ctrl+Alt+F3 for a text screen; log in and type sudo reboot.
If even that doesn't respond: hold Alt and SysRq (Print Screen) and press, slowly, R E I S U B — a safe forced restart.
A short press of the power button asks the system to shut down cleanly; only holding it cuts the power.
unclean.source: Linux kernel documentation, sysrq; the 2026-09-29 case

I101.title: A system service failed
I101.meaning: These services failed to start or stopped with an error: {units}.

causes.failed_unit: A service reported a failure; its own log says why.

failed_unit.words: Look at the service's own message.
failed_unit.explain: Shows whether the service runs and its last log lines. It only reads.

S101.title: An update was left unfinished
S101.meaning: The package database says an installation didn't finish (for example after a power cut during an update).

causes.interrupted: An install or update was interrupted.

steps: Open Update Manager: it offers to fix it.
interrupted.explain: Finishes setting up packages that were unpacked but not configured. It doesn't download or remove anything.
